does: Turns the fat and the softened onions or the browned bits left in a pan into a smooth pouring sauce: flour is cooked straight into the fat, and hot stock is stirred in little by little and simmered until it thickens.
how: Leave a little fat in the pan with the onions or the browned bits.
Stir in a spoonful of flour and cook it for a moment, so that it loses its raw taste.
Pour in hot stock a little at a time, stirring hard after each addition to keep it smooth.
Simmer until the gravy coats a spoon but still pours, and season it at the end.

cues.text: A glossy gravy that coats the back of a spoon and runs off it in a steady stream.
Savoury and rounded, with no floury taste.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in all the stock at once, so that the flour forms lumps.
mistakes.fix: Add it a little at a time and stir until smooth before adding more.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling it down too far, so that it turns thick and gluey.
mistakes.fix: Loosen it with a splash more stock or water.

comes_after.why: Onion gravy starts from onions fried soft and golden in the pan.

variant_of.differs: The flour is cooked straight into the fat and onions in the pan, not made as a separate roux, and the sauce is kept loose enough to pour and soak into mash.
